messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: (patient's name)
Age: 84 years old
Gender: Female
Admission Date: (date of admission)
Discharge Date: (date of discharge)
Length of Stay: (number of days of hospital stay)
Clinical Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted due to her underlying medical conditions including type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She also had a history of amblyopia OD and a resolved branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) in the left eye. During her hospital stay, she was treated with Eyefolate™ capsules and no further complications were reported during the course of treatment.

Clinical Progress:
In October 2013, the patient's best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/150 OD and 20/25 OS. The OS fundus photo showed a large macular aneurysm (MA) in the superior temporal region with exudates. After being prescribed the Eyefolate™ capsules, the BCVA of the left eye improved to 20/20 in August 2014. Further improvement was seen in December 2014 when the large exudates almost completely resolved in OS (Fig. b). In January 2016, the BCVA was 20/400 OD and 20/25 OS, and the MA was resolved as shown in the OS fundus photo (Fig. c) during 2016.

Follow-up:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition with instructions to continue taking prescribed medications and regular follow-up appointments with her primary care physician to monitor her diabetes and hypertension. A referral to an ophthalmologist was also recommended to monitor her vision and perpetuate the effectiveness of the treatment.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this episode is the retinal arterial macroaneurysm with exudates in the left eye, which was the condition actually treated (with Eyefolate). This is an eye disorder in chapter H, coded as a retinal vascular change in category H35, rather than diabetic retinopathy or the underlying hypertension.

CODE: H35
